cvEn:
Shlomo (Momo) Laniado, son of Linda and Gavriel, was born on the 19th of Sivan 5713 (2 June 1953) in Tel Aviv. He attended the "Ledugma" elementary school named after Henrietta Szold in Tel Aviv, and afterward continued his studies at Ironi Dalet High School and the "Pitman" commercial school. Shlomo was a good student, liked by his teachers and friends. He was a member of the Tzofim (Israeli Scouts) movement, and in later years he led the movement's Tel Aviv troop, where he was the driving spirit. He organized the hikes and camps, the training, and the sailing competitions, and he worked hard repairing the boats and refinishing and painting them. He loved the sea and would go swimming in every season, in summer and in winter. He was also a photography enthusiast and enjoyed handicrafts. He read many books on a wide range of subjects and listened to music in his free time. He was a volunteer firefighter.

Shlomo was sociable and easy to befriend. As a person who knew how to read others, he never held a grudge against anyone. He always kept away from quarrels and strife and did everything he could to make peace, patiently explaining the importance of compromise and forgiveness. Helping others, loyalty, and keeping a confidence were principles from which he never strayed. His kindness was known among his friends. He answered every request willingly and cheerfully, even when it was inconvenient for him. Shlomo enjoyed conversation and discussing all kinds of topics; his words were always reasoned and tasteful, seasoned with humor and laughter. Even difficult and heavy things he said to his friends, he said with a smile and with care, so as not to hurt them. He was modest and content with what he had, he loved simplicity and did not seek to stand out. He was hardworking and diligent, thorough and persistent, enterprising and skilled with his hands.

Shlomo was drafted into the IDF in early February 1972 and assigned to the Armored Corps. After basic training he completed the course for the "Patton" tank, where he was an outstanding trainee and received a high grade (95). He then took the course for Patton tank commanders. Shortly before the war broke out, he began a course for officers of the Armored Corps. He was responsible and devoted to his role, cared for his soldiers, and they loved him very much. He was not strict about formal discipline, but he demanded precise performance from his soldiers. For his part in operational activity he was awarded the "Operational Service Medal." Throughout his service he tried not to worry his family and made sure to write letters home. When the Yom Kippur War broke out, he was sent with his unit to the front in Sinai, where he took part in the battles to block the Egyptians, who had crossed the Suez Canal. On 8 October 1973, Shlomo's tank was hit directly by two missiles in a battle in the central sector, opposite Ismailia. He suffered severe burns and died of his wounds on the 26th of Tishrei 5734 (22 October 1973). His comrades recount that he fought with composure and encouraged his soldiers with a smile. He was laid to rest in the Kiryat Shaul cemetery. He is survived by his parents and two sisters. After his death he was promoted to Second Lieutenant.
